desc: This surface area calculator calculates the surface area of a sphere, cube, cylinder, pyramid, cone, and rectangular and triangular prism.

m.h: Surface area will be calculated for the selected shape.

c: Surface area refers to the total area of the outer surfaces of a 3D shape.
Sphere’s surface area formula S = 4 × π × r2
Cylinder’s surface area formula Total: S = 2 ×π × r2 + 2 × π × r × h Base: π × r2 Lateral: 2 × π × r × h
Cube’s surface area formula S = 6 × a2
Cone’s surface area formula Total: S = π × r2 + π × r × l Lateral: π × r × l Base: π × r2 Note: l = √(r2 + h2)
Rectangular prism’s surface area formula S = 2(l × w + l × h + w × h)
Triangular prism’s surface area formula Total: S = 2 × B + (a + b + c) × h Lateral: (a + b + c) × h Base: B = √[p(p − a)(p − b)(p − c)] with p = (a + b + c​) / 2
Pyramid’s surface area formula (equilateral triangle base) S = (√3 / 4) × a² + (3 × a × l) / 2 Note: h = √(l2 − ((√3 × a) / 6)2)
Pyramid’s surface area formula (square base) S = a2 + 2 × a × l Note: h = √(l2 − (a / 2)2)
Pyramid’s surface area formula (rectangle base) Total: S = a × b + a × √(h2 + (a / 2)2) + b × √(h2 + (b / 2)2)
Pyramid’s surface area formula (pentagon base) S = (5 × a2) / (4 × tan(π / 5)) + (5 × a × l) / 2 Note: h = √(l2 − (a / (2 × tan(π / 5)))2)
Pyramid’s surface area formula (hexagon base) S = (3 × √3 × a2) / 2 + 3 × a × l Note: h = √(l2 − ((√3 × a) / 2)2)
Hemisphere’s surface area formula S = 3 × π × r2
Capsule’s surface area formula S = 2 × π × r × h + 4 × π × r2
Spherical cap’s surface area formula Total: S = 2 × π × r × h + π × a2 Lateral = 2 × π × r × h Base = π × a2

desc: Simplify geometry with our surface area of a rectangular prism calculator, applying the surface area of a rectangular prism formula for accurate results.

eq.formula: area = 2 * length * width + 2 * length * height + 2 * width * height

name: Surface area to volume ratio
title: Surface Area to Volume Ratio Calculator
desc: Surface area to volume ratio calculator helps you determine the amount of surface an object has relative to its size. It is a great tool to predict how reactive a process can be if you increase its surface area.

eq.formula: ConSA = pi * Conrad * (Conrad+ (Conheight * Conheight + Conrad * Conrad)^0.5)
CapSA = 4 * pi * Caprad^2 +  2 * pi * Caprad * Capheight
TPSA =0.5 * sqrt(TP1 * TP2 * TP3 * TP4) + TPheight * TP1
RPSA = 2 * (RPlen * RPwidth + RPheight * RPwidth + RPlen * RPheight)
CFSA = pi * ( CFrad1^2 + CFrad2^2 + (CFrad1 + CFrad2) * ((CFrad1 - CFrad2)^2 + CFheight^2)^0.5)

var.f: PI*(pow(CFrad1, 2) + CFrad1*sqrt(pow(CFheight, 2) + pow(CFrad1 - CFrad2, 2)) + pow(CFrad2, 2) + CFrad2*sqrt(pow(CFheight, 2) + pow(CFrad1 - CFrad2, 2)))

eq.formula: CFvol = (1/3) * pi * CFheight * (CFrad1^2 + CFrad1 * CFrad2 + CFrad2^2)
FSSA =  FSa^2 + FSb^2 + 2 * (FSa + FSb) * ( FS1+ FSh^2 )^0.5

var.f: -sqrt(FS1 + pow(FSh, 2)) + sqrt(FS1 + FSSA - pow(FSb, 2) - 2*FSb*sqrt(FS1 + pow(FSh, 2)) + pow(FSh, 2))
-sqrt(FS1 + pow(FSh, 2)) + sqrt(FS1 + FSSA - pow(FSa, 2) - 2*FSa*sqrt(FS1 + pow(FSh, 2)) + pow(FSh, 2))
